newsitem.title: USA: US WEST COAST CRUDES FALL, ALASKAN CRUDE SELLS.
newsitem.headline: US WEST COAST CRUDES FALL, ALASKAN CRUDE SELLS.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices declined Thursday with other oil markets despite a shrinking discount for benchmark Alaskan grade, traders said.

A West Coast refiner sold Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude -- the regional benchmark -- at $1.97 a barrel under September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI) crude for delivery next month, traders said.
The refiner, which typically buys ANS, sold the cargo because it replaced its ANS supply with Colombian South Blend, traders said.
The discount has shrunk since a mid-June cargo at minus $2.08, then held at that level for over a month as refiners saw weak gasoline prices diminish their buying power.
"Margins are good right now, so refiners can afford to pay that," a trader said.

Analysts reported that profits on gasoline for West Coast refiners improved 25 percent in the second half of July. Meanwhile, Thursday's spot price for WTI dropped 37 cents a barrel to $20.09 as traders expected supplies to increase when Iraqi resumed oil exports in the coming days, traders said.
Kern River and Wilmington grades remained flat, with no deals reported.
